title: Functional Analysis of Membrane Proteins Produced by Cell-Free Translation
author: Srujan Kumar Dondapati
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bpsqmndw

steps.title: Prepare MSP protein solution
steps.instruction: Make a 5 mg · mL⁻¹ (200 µM) MSP protein solution in 20 mM Tris, pH 7.4, containing 0.1 M NaCl and 0.5 mM EDTA.

steps.title: Dissolve lipids in cholate
steps.instruction: Dissolve DMPC, DOTAP and DOPG lipids in cholate buffer to a final concentration of 15 mM (see Note 2).

steps.title: Form lipid‑MSP mixture and add biobeads
steps.instruction: Incubate the lipid‑MSP mixture at 25 °C for 30 min. Add SM‑2 Biobeads to reach ~80 vol % of the mixture and incubate further at 25 °C for 45 min. Centrifuge at 1 000 × g for 1 min (temperature as indicated) and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Second biobead treatment and final clarification
steps.instruction: Add a second aliquot of SM‑2 Biobeads (80 vol %) to each reaction, incubate 15 min, then centrifuge at 1 000 × g, room temperature, 1 min and collect the top solution. Centrifuge this solution at 5 000 × g for 5 min (temperature as indicated); keep the top liquid while leaving the lower ~5 µL behind. This clarified solution is used for zetasizer analysis.

steps.title: Measure nanodisc size
steps.instruction: Place 20 µL of the recovered solution in a Zetasizer cuvette and record the size‑intensity distribution; a strong peak near 11.5 nm indicates nanodiscs.

steps.title: Set up cell‑free synthesis of BR/MtlA
steps.instruction: Prepare 50 µL cell‑free reactions containing 35 % (v/v) E. coli lysate with T7 RNA‑polymerase, 40 % (v/v reaction buffer with 1.2 mM each amino acid), 1 µL 25× XE‑solution (EasyXpress), plasmid at 0.75 µg · mL⁻¹, 14C‑leucine at 50 µM (4 DPM · pmol⁻¹), and 10 % (v/v) prepared nanodiscs. Include parallel control reactions without nanodiscs.

steps.title: Run cell‑free translation
steps.instruction: Incubate the reactions in a thermomixer shaking at 500 rpm, 37 °C for 1 h 30 min.

steps.title: Collect samples for analysis
steps.instruction: From each completed reaction, withdraw 2 × 5 µL of the suspension for TCA precipitation and 1 × 5 µL for SDS‑PAGE. Centrifuge the remaining mixture at 16 000 × g, 4 °C, 10 min. Collect the supernatant; from it take 2 × 5 µL for TCA precipitation and 1 × 5 µL for SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: TCA precipitation of protein
steps.instruction: Mix each 5 µL aliquot (suspension or supernatant) with 3 mL trichloroacetic acid (TCA). Incubate in a water bath at 80 °C for 15 min, then place on ice for 30 min.

steps.title: Filter and wash precipitated protein
steps.instruction: Filter the TCA‑precipitated mixture using a vacuum filtration system to retain radiolabeled protein on the filter paper. Wash the filter twice with TCA and twice with acetone. Air‑dry the filter papers for a few minutes under a fume hood.

steps.title: Scintillation counting
steps.instruction: Transfer each dried, protein‑laden filter paper to a scintillation tube, add 3 mL scintillation cocktail, shake on an orbital shaker for at least 1 h, and measure 14C‑leucine incorporation with a liquid scintillation counter.

steps.title: Prepare SDS‑PAGE samples
steps.instruction: For each 5 µL aliquot, add 45 µL water and 150 µL ice‑cold acetone, incubate on ice for 15 min, then centrifuge at 16 000 × g, 4 °C, 10 min. Discard the acetone supernatant.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE and visualize
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 20 µL NuPAGE® LDS Sample Buffer, load onto precast SDS‑PAGE gels, run at 200 V for 35 min, dry gels at 70 °C for 1 h 10 min, and detect radiolabeled proteins with a phosphorimager.

steps.title: UV‑Vis analysis of BR
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance spectrum of the BR‑containing supernatant (Step 10) from 400–600 nm; a peak around 550 nm (purple color) confirms correctly folded BR.

steps.title: Transcribe mRNA for KcsA
steps.instruction: Incubate plasmid DNA (60 µg · mL⁻¹) or E‑PCR product (8 µg · mL⁻¹) with 80 mM HEPES‑KOH (pH 7.6), 15 mM MgCl₂, 3.75 mM NTPs, 0.5 mM m⁷G(ppp)G‑CAP analog, and 1 U · µL⁻¹ T7 RNA polymerase at 37 °C for 2 h. Purify the mRNA using DyeEx spin columns and quantify with a NanoDrop 2000c.

steps.title: Translate KcsA protein
steps.instruction: Add the purified mRNA to a final concentration of 260 µg · mL⁻¹ in the translation mix, include 14C‑leucine to 60 µM, and incubate 1 h 30 min at 27 °C.

steps.title: Analyze KcsA translation products
steps.instruction: Perform TCA precipitation (Steps 9‑11) and SDS‑PAGE (Steps 12‑13) on the KcsA translation reactions as described for BR/MtlA.

steps.title: Prepare vesicular fraction (VF)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 50 µL of the translation mixture at 16 000 × g, 4 °C, 10 min. Separate the supernatant (SN) and retain the pellet (VF) containing microsomes.

steps.title: Wash vesicular fraction
steps.instruction: Resuspend VF in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.0 by pipetting up and down, centrifuge again under the same conditions, and repeat once; keep the final VF pellet.

steps.title: Detergent‑resuspend VF
steps.instruction: Dissolve the washed VF pellet in 50 µL cholate buffer and vortex vigorously.

steps.title: Reconstitute VF with lipids
steps.instruction: Mix 50 µL detergent‑resuspended VF with 50 µL 15 mM lipid solution (e.g., DOPG), rotate at 300 rpm, 4 °C for 1 h.

steps.title: Remove detergent with Biobeads
steps.instruction: Add SM‑2 Biobeads to reach ~80 vol % of the lipid mixture and incubate overnight (≈16 h) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Collect proteoliposomes
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge to pellet the Biobeads, collect the supernatant containing proteoliposomes, and store at 4 °C (stable for several days).

steps.title: Puromycin treatment for sec61 assay
steps.instruction: Add 30 µL of 2.5 mM puromycin in 500 mM KCl to the VF, incubate on ice 45 min to reach 250 µM puromycin in 500 mM KCl, then centrifuge at 16 000 × g, 4 °C, 10 min, discard SN, and prepare proteoliposomes as in Steps 21‑23.

steps.title: Prepare lipid stocks
steps.instruction: Dissolve desired lipids in octane to 2 mg · mL⁻¹ and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Form planar lipid bilayer on MECA chip
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL electrolyte solution to the measurement chamber of the MECA array chip. Pipette ~0.1 µL DPhPC (2 mg · mL⁻¹ in octane) onto the chip surface and paint it by moving a magnetic bar across the apertures with a slow rotation (45–180° · s⁻¹).

steps.title: Confirm bilayer formation
steps.instruction: Observe the resistance change from MΩ to GΩ, indicating successful bilayer formation (see Notes 8‑9).

steps.title: Fuse proteoliposomes to bilayer
steps.instruction: Add 4 µL of the proteoliposomes (puromycin‑treated microsomes, no protein synthesized) to the buffer chamber containing the bilayer and allow fusion to occur.

steps.title: Record single‑channel activity
steps.instruction: Voltage‑clamp the bilayer and record currents with an EPC‑10 single‑channel amplifier and Patchmaster software (sampling 50 kHz, 10 kHz Bessel filter).

steps.title: Analyze electrophysiology data
steps.instruction: Process voltage‑ramp and single‑channel recordings using Patchmaster and Clampfit v10.7 to extract parameters such as conductance, open probability, and sub‑conductance states.
